To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the properties of GRB-DLA absorbers are consistent with the predictions of high resolution simulations of hierarchical galaxy formation.
the properties of GRB-DLA absorbers are similar to QSO-DLAS, except that the former are more massive and have higher star formation rates.

the incidence of low HI columns in GRB aftergows is higher than predicted by current simulations and that the mean metallicity of HI absorbers is consistent with that of the stellar population of their hosts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical interpretation of the properties of intrinsic Lyα absorption lines seen in the spectra.
the physical interpretation of GRB afterglow spectra.
the physical properties of the interstellar medium of GRB-DLA hosts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the properties of GRB-DLA absorbers are consistent with those expected for gas in protogalactic halos.
GRB-DLA and QSO-DLA absorbers are similar in many ways, but the former are more likely to be found in higher mass halos, have higher star formation rates and are more metal rich.
GRB-DLA absorbers are similar to, but more metal enriched than, QSO-DLAS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the properties of GRB-DLA absorbers, as predicted by the simulations of galaxy formation, are in reasonable agreement with observations.

the properties of GRB-DLA absorbers are consistent with the idea that they are formed in the same halos that host QSO-DLAS, and are therefore likely to share many of the properties of the QSO-DLA population.
our simulations reproduce many key aspects of GRB-DLA spectra, and provide a framework for understanding their physical origins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast to QSO-DLAS, GRB-DLASs are associated with halos that are more metal rich, have higher star formation rates, and have higher gas metallicities.
GRB hosts are more massive than those of QSOs, and this difference is likely to be reflected in the properties of the gas in the two classes of absorbers.

the properties of GRB-DLA absorbers are broadly consistent with the predictions of hierarchical galaxy formation models and that GRB-DLA studies can be used to probe the properties of the low-mass end of the galaxy population.
